1	# Support Team Member Time Off
2	
3	
4	## Support Team Member Time Off
5	
6	The Support Team follows [GitLab's paid time off policy](/handbook/people-group/time-off-and-absence/time-off-types/).
7	We balance that with the need to deliver support to our customers every day.
8	This page is intended to provide all Support Team Members with an understanding
9	of what we need to do to achieve that balance, making it possible for all to
10	take time off as needed and desired, while we as a team continue to deliver
11	amazing support and service to our customers.
12	
13	There is a special point that needs to be emphasized, and that is that time off
14	for any team member only serves its purpose *if that person truly takes the time
15	off*. Nobody should feel pressure or the need to check Slack, email, or anything
16	else associated with work during their time off. **Especially when you are taking
17	time to be on holiday or to be with family or friends, please, in the timeless
18	words of the snow queen, Elsa, "let it go."**
19

63	## Choosing and recording time off
64	
65	Please take time off whenever you need it.
66	
67	A little thoughtfulness on everybody's part will go a long way toward making it
68	possible for everyone to take their desired days off. As you look to plan your
69	time off, please:
70	
71	- ensure you know the [company wide paid time off guidelines](/handbook/people-group/time-off-and-absence/time-off-types/)
72	- consider a different time off schedule if your [regional capacity calendar](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-com/support/toolbox/support-calendar) shows that on any of the days you would be absent, the regional team would be short by 20% or more of its people
73	- check the regional calendar and coordinate with your manager to ensure we have sufficient cover for days with low availability. You can do this by ensuring that you are subscribed to your associated regional calendar (i.e., `EMEA - OOO`, `AMER - OOO`, `APAC - OOO`) and that prior to booking time off, you check the calendar:
74	  - 🟩 Green: You're good to book PTO.
75	  - 🟨 Yellow: The team is nearing PTO capacity – consider other dates if possible.
76	  - 🟥 Red: PTO capacity has been reached. Please discuss with your manager before proceeding.
77	  - the calendar colors are determined by the percentage of engineers on PTO:
78	  - 🟢 Green: 0–15% of engineers on PTO
79	  - 🟡 Yellow: >15% to 20% of engineers on PTO
80	  - 🔴 Red: >20% of engineers on PTO
81	- schedule your time off as far in advance as you can, especially for days that may be popular, are [holidays](#how-support-handles-holidays), or that are particularly important to you
82	- don't lock yourself into nonrefundable travel itineraries before you've taken steps such as the above to be sure you can get the planned days off
83	- if possible, plan your time off to avoid disruptions to the various rotations such as on-call
84	
85	## Preparing for time off
86	
87	When you are approaching a planned absence from work, it is your responsibility
88	to take reasonable actions to prepare the team and your customers for your
89	absence. By making these preparations, you will also be making it easier for
90	yourself to disconnect from work and make your time off effective.
91	
92	If you're taking off **less than half a day,** you do not need to make entries in Workday or the Support Time Off Calendar, but please consider updating your Slack status. Also consider blocking the interval on your personal Google Calendar, so no one tries to book a pairing/meeting with you during that time.
93	
94	If you're taking off **a half day or more,** enter the time off in Workday.
95	
96	Follow the guidance below to prepare yourself, your customers, and your colleagues.
97	
98	### Coverage for roles
99	
100	If you are assigned to any PagerDuty shifts (such as on-call) during the time off, arrange for coverage:
101	
102	1. Find a volunteer to cover for you; get help from your manager if necessary.
103	1. [Create the appropriate override in PagerDuty](https://support.pagerduty.com/main/docs/edit-schedules#create-overrides).
104	
105	### Coverage for assigned tickets
106	
107	Tidy your queue before going on PTO. As guidelines cannot cover every case,
108	this section is meant to provide guidance for you to think critically about
109	what is required to ensure continued excellent support for each customer with
110	whom you're working on a ticket.
111	
112	#### If your absence will be less than three business days
113	
114	If your PTO will prevent a timely update, ask the customer whether
115	they would prefer to pause the ticket with the `on-hold` status or
116	have someone else step in.
117	For high priority tickets, tend towards a handing over to someone else:
118	
119	1. Use the [OOO Ticket Summary](https://gitlab.com/search?search=360080271299&group_id=2573624&project_id=17008590&scope=&search_code=true&snippets=false&repository_ref=master&nav_source=navbar)
120	   macro, providing the same information as described in the
121	   [Workflow](/handbook/support/workflows/ooo-ticket-management#workflow)
122	   topic of the `OOO Ticket Management` page.
123	
124	#### If your absence is three or more business days
125	
126	1. Change your workflow in advance of your absence:
127	   1. A week in advance: Start thinking about whether you may need to hand off tickets, and pair with others to get them up to speed.
128	   1. One day in advance: Stop assigning new tickets with your own region as the preferred region. Instead, prioritize FRT-stage tickets from other regions that you can respond to initially and then reassign (reHome) after your first reply.
129	   1. Work to resolve and close as many of your assigned tickets as possible.
130	   1. Contribute more to first responses and other people's tickets - internal comments, pairing
131	      sessions - to make up for not taking new tickets of your own.
132	1. Follow the [OOO Ticket Management](/handbook/support/workflows/ooo-ticket-management)
133	   process to arrange for others to take care of your tickets in your absence.
134	1. To ensure you're not auto-assigned to GDPR requests in case of an extented leave (e.g 2 weeks or longer):
135	
136	   - Update the corresponding `yaml` file for yourself in the [Support Team project](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-support-readiness/support-team/-/tree/master/data/agents).
137	   - Change `works_account_deletion: true` to `works_account_deletion: false`
138	   - Request a review from your manager.
139	   - Make sure to undo this change when you return from OOO.
140	1. After coming back, make sure to follow the guidelines for [catching up after a scheduled time off](#catching-up-after-a-scheduled-time-off).
141	
142	## How Support Handles Family and Friends Days
143	
144	During [Family and Friends Days](/handbook/company/family-and-friends-day/#upcoming-family-and-friends-days) GitLab Support continues
145	to operate as normal. In FY26, you are free to take off a total of 4 days at your convenience, to celebrate and record as Family and Friends day.
146	Please follow the same guidelines as you would in [Choosing and Recording Time Off](#choosing-and-recording-time-off).
147	
148	## How Support Handles Holidays
149	
150	During Holidays, GitLab Support continues to operate as normal. Always book holidays as required by your locality. For
151	non-statutory holidays, please follow the same guidelines as you would in [Choosing and Recording Time Off](#choosing-and-recording-time-off).
152	
153	From late November through the first week of January, "the holiday season,"
154	each Support region takes additional steps to coordinate time off so that they
155	will maintain sufficient staffing levels to meet customer needs.
156	
157	### APAC
158	
159	APAC plans for several high-impact holiday periods.  Details of these dates are noted in the [APAC support page](/handbook/support/apac/#holiday-coverage-planning).
160	
161	For end of year coverage, planning begins in September-October.
162	
163	This typically involves determining the appropriate coverage based on both the volume of incoming tickets during the holiday period the previous year, and the general ticket volume trend since then.
164	
165	The team then sign up in the planning issue to provide the necessary coverage by the end of October. This allows time for discussion if anything is at risk.
166	
167	Other factors taken into account for coverage include:
168	
169	- L&R expertise
170	- CEOC, CMOC & Support-Manager on-call coverage - we prefer people covering on-call roles to be working rather than doing it while they are on PTO, so we'll generally seek to swap shifts with those providing coverage
171	- region coverage - as a wide region, we need to ensure we have sufficient people on in both the first and second halves of the APAC day
172	- shift coverage for 24/7 support
173	
174	Previous planning issues can be seen in this [epic](https://gitlab.com/groups/gitlab-com/support/-/epics/252).
175	
176	### EMEA
177	
178	The EMEA Support Team plans coverage for several high-impact holiday periods throughout the year, with the two primary planning periods being Easter and the End of year Holiday season.
179	
180	For each of these periods, EMEA Support Managers will create planning issues such as:
181	
182	- [EMEA Year End Coverage 2025 - 2026](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-com/support/support-team-meta/-/issues/7194) - planning usually begins 6-8 weeks in advance
183	- [EMEA Coverage Planning - Easter Long Weekend and the surrounding 2 weeks](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-com/support/support-team-meta/-/issues/5806) - planning usually begins in October
184	
185	These planning issues include an associated spreadsheet where Support Engineers can share their holiday plans and coordinate coverage. This approach ensures:
186	
187	- Adequate coverage across all EMEA time zones during holiday periods
188	- Visibility of team availability well in advance
189	- Fair distribution of holiday time off
190	- Sufficient expertise coverage (L&R, CEOC, CMOC, and on-call roles)
191	
192	Team members are encouraged to add their plans to the spreadsheet as early as possible to facilitate better coordination. While the team aims to accommodate all requested time off, Support Engineers should avoid making firm commitments (such as purchasing nonrefundable travel) until coverage has been confirmed by the management team.
193	
194	### AMER
195	
196	AMER Support Managers will create and publish an issue in late September, using
197	[this template](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-com/support/support-team-meta/-/blob/master/.gitlab/issue_templates/Year%20end%20holiday%20coverage%20AMER.md?ref_type=heads).
198	In that issue they will invite everyone in AMER Support to use a specified Google
199	Form to indicate their preferences for days off during the holiday season. Once
200	the form has closed, around the 15th of October, the AMER Support managers will
201	quickly determine whether any changes need to be made to anybody's requested
202	days off.
203	
204	While it's not very likely that anyone will be asked to work on a day that they
205	would like to take off, it is possible. For that reason, please don't make any
206	firm commitments (such as purchasing a nonrefundable travel itinerary) until
207	the management team sends out notice that the schedule is confirmed.
208	
209	### Holiday time off ticket management
210	
211	Guidance around ticket handling over global holiday time off is slightly different, because of the potentially increased impact on the Support team.
212	
213	The following peak holidays have the greatest potential to affect coverage:
214	
215	- Australia Day (26-January)
216	- Republic Day (26-January)
217	- Anzac Day (25-April)
218	- International Workers Day (1-May)
219	- Memorial Day (last Monday in May)
220	- Independence Day (1-July to 4-July)
221	- U.S. Thanksgiving Day (4th Thursday of November)
222	- Immaculate Conception Day (8-Dec)
223	- Christmas Day, St Stephens Day, Boxing Day, New Years Day and Day After New Years (Period between 24-Dec to 2-Jan)
224	- Holidays that vary in dates each year that are celebrated in multiple countries:
225	  - Easter Sunday (late March to early April)
226	  - Easter Monday (late March to early April)
227	  - Whit Monday (May or June)
228	  - Ascension Day (May)
229	  - Labour Day (first Monday in September)
230	
231	**NOTE: For AMER holidays and coverage requirements, see [AMER Holiday Coverage Targets](/handbook/support/amer/#amer-holiday-coverage-targets)**.
232	
233	### If you are planning to take time off during peak holidays
234	
235	If you plan to be out for more than three days, follow the guidance regarding
236	[absences of three or more business days](#if-your-absence-is-three-or-more-business-days).
237	Otherwise:
238	
239	1. Please do your best to resolve any assigned tickets you have in your queue.
240	1. Communicate with your customers to let them know the days you'll be away, and
241	   to ask whether they will need help during your absence. Many of our customers
242	   might be on the same holiday schedule and will be fine with resuming work on
243	   a ticket when you both return.
244	1. For those tickets that will not require action over the holiday, there is no
245	   special action to be taken.
246	
247	### If you are working on a holiday
248	
249	1. Continue to prioritize FRT first, and then management of your own tickets.
250	1. Please pay **extra** attention to NRT on tickets with an assignee who is currently out-of-office.
251	
252	## General Tips
253	
254	In addition to the company-wide tips in
255	[Communicating Your Time Off](/handbook/people-group/time-off-and-absence/time-off-types/),
256	take a look at these tips to increase your ability to disconnect from work,
257	truly make the most of your time off, and make it easier to return to work:
258	
259	1. Unsubscribe from any MRs that will likely resolve while you're away, and then
260	   you won't have to deal with all the emails from them when you return.
261	1. Set up some email filters to move emails into buckets that you can address
262	   one-at-a-time when you return.
263	1. Disconnect yourself from Slack and Gmail in any of these ways:
264	   *NOTE: Time Off by Deel is supposed to turn off Slack notifications on your phone and
265	   set DND mode. But just in case, you may want to do one of these:*
266	   1. log out from Slack and Gmail on your phone, or
267	   1. remove Slack and Gmail from your phone, or
268	   1. pause the Slack and Gmail apps on your phone
269	   1. manually configure Slack and Gmail to send no notifications on your phone
270	
271	## Re-connect after time off
272	
273	Please consider adding an item in the Support Week in Review after you get back to let the rest of the
274	team know what you've been up to!
275	
276	## Catching up after a scheduled time off
277	
278	Trying to catch-up after a scheduled time off - especially if it's a week long, or more - can be a bit overwhelming.
279	So here is a list of resources to check that should get you up to date with almost everything
280	that happened while you were away:
281	
282	- [Support Week in Review (SWIR)](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-com/support/readiness/support-week-in-review/-/issues/?sort=created_date&state=closed&label_name%5B%5D=SWIR%3A%3ADigest&first_page_size=20)
283	
284	- Slack channels:
285	  - [#company-fyi](https://gitlab.slack.com/archives/C010XFJFTHN)
286	  - [#company-fyi-private](https://gitlab.slack.com/archives/C02E7JGBU4E)
287	  - [#whats-happening-at-gitlab](https://gitlab.slack.com/archives/C0259241C)
288	
289	Consider setting up a few coffee chats with teammates to simply reconnect with them. You can also ask your teammates who haven't taken PTO while you were out, during coffee chats or pairing sessions, to mention a thing or two that you might have missed.
290	
291	If you unassigned some of your tickets before going on PTO, take the time to go through them and check their status. It's good practice to reassign them to yourself if these are either still missing a DRI, or if it appears that you're still the best equipped person to drive it to a solution.
292	
293	## Managers Time Off
294	
295	### Before PTO is taken
296	
297	The manager will conduct a thorough review of all ongoing tasks, responsibilities, and projects.
298	
299	1. List Key Responsibilities: The manager will prepare a comprehensive list of all tasks that require attention during their absence.
300	1. Determine Priority: The manager will assess which tasks are time-sensitive and which can be delayed. They will prioritize duties based on urgency, impact, and team dependency.
301	1. Select a Delegate: The manager will choose a single team member to be responsible for all of the tasks, or another manager if any of the tasks are confidential.
302	
303	### Task Delegation
304	
305	Once tasks have been identified and the team member has been selected, the following steps should be taken to ensure a seamless transition:
306	
307	Documenting the Process: The manager will create an issue to outline
308	
309	- Key contacts for each task.
310	- Any ongoing projects or deadlines.
311	- Specific instructions or checklists to be followed.
312	- Access to Resources: Ensure that the delegate has the necessary access to tools, files, and systems to perform tasks effectively.
313	
314	### Communicate
315	
316	The manager will inform the team and relevant stakeholders about the temporary delegation of responsibilities.
317	
318	### After PTO
319	
320	Conduct a Debriefing: The manager will meet with the team member to review the progress made, any challenges encountered, and the outcomes of decisions made in their absence.
321	
322	For more tips, check [returning from pto](/handbook/people-group/time-off-and-absence/time-off-types/).
323	
324	## Shift Engineer Time Off
325	
326	### Planning Coverage for Time Off
327	
328	Before their time off, Shift Engineers should find coverage for their weekend shifts. The following people should be considered first for covering shifts:
329	
330	1. Other Shift Engineers.
331	1. Support Engineers in the CEOC role leading up to the weekend.
332	1. Other Support Engineers, or ask a Manager for assistance finding coverage.
333	
334	Coverage is only required for weekends days being taken off. All other days can follow the normal time off recommendations.
335	
336	### Sick Time
337	
338	If you are sick, [page the on-call Support Manager](/handbook/support/on-call/#engaging-the-on-call-manager) as soon as you know you will be out on a weekend.
339	
340	### Guidelines for Covering a Weekend Shift
341	
342	If you are covering for a Shift Engineer, be mindful of what tickets are allowed to have [public replies](/handbook/support/workflows/working-on-tickets/#weekend-focus-for-shift-engineers) posted during a weekend.
343	
344	### Holidays as a Shift Engineer
345	
346	If a holiday occurs on a weekend, and you'd like to take it off, follow the guidance to plan coverage for your time off.
347	
348	You are also welcome to work the holiday, and float the holiday time to another day of your choosing. It's recommended that you float the holiday to any day within one month before or after the holiday.
349

# Support Team Member Time Off


## Support Team Member Time Off

The Support Team follows [GitLab's paid time off policy](/handbook/people-group/time-off-and-absence/time-off-types/).
We balance that with the need to deliver support to our customers every day.
This page is intended to provide all Support Team Members with an understanding
of what we need to do to achieve that balance, making it possible for all to
take time off as needed and desired, while we as a team continue to deliver
amazing support and service to our customers.

There is a special point that needs to be emphasized, and that is that time off
for any team member only serves its purpose *if that person truly takes the time
off*. Nobody should feel pressure or the need to check Slack, email, or anything
else associated with work during their time off. **Especially when you are taking
time to be on holiday or to be with family or friends, please, in the timeless
words of the snow queen, Elsa, "let it go."**

### One-time setup actions

#### Support Time Off calendars

1. Be sure you have access to the
[**Support - Time Off**](https://calendar.google.com/calendar/embed?src=gitlab.com_as6a088eo3mrvbo57n5kddmgdg%40group.calendar.google.com)
team calendar.
   1. You should have been granted access during Support Onboarding. If you don't have it, verify whether you are part of the Support Google Group (supportteam@); if you are not, ask to be added (as per the role based entitlements) via the #support_operations Slack channel (cc @jcolyer).

1. Set up the Google Calendar integration with Time Off by Deel, so that you do not need to populate your personal and "Support - Time Off" calendars manually.
   1. In Slack, click the `+` sign next to 'Apps' at the bottom of the left sidebar
   1. Search for 'Time Off by Deel' and click 'View'
   1. Under 'Home', click on 'Your Events' to show a dropdown
   1. Click on 'Calendar Sync' under the Settings break
   1. Click on 'Connect your Calendar' and complete the actions to sync your calendar to Time Off by Deel
      - You will see a 'Success! Your calendar has been connected.' message and
        your calendar listed under 'Your synced calendar' in Time Off by Deel on Slack
      - ***NOTE: this also serves to block your availability in Calendly, and ensures your OOO is included in the [regional capacity calendars](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-com/support/toolbox/support-calendar)***
   1. After your personal calendar is linked, click 'Add calendar' under
   'Additional calendars to include?'. The 'Support - Time Off' calendar ID is
   `gitlab.com_as6a088eo3mrvbo57n5kddmgdg@group.calendar.google.com`
1. Verify the following calendars are shared with you. These are shared with the Support Team Google Group:
   1. [Support OOO - AMER](https://calendar.google.com/calendar/embed?src=c_9166d2302886c4ae23f34099eeb4015e2d520e1dd4029711becd8370be996513%40group.calendar.google.com)
   1. [Support OOO - APAC](https://calendar.google.com/calendar/embed?src=c_408bhp8a8j579lqr99j552u21s%40group.calendar.google.com)
   1. [Support OOO - EMEA](https://calendar.google.com/calendar/u/0/embed?src=c_ev56c9rgjd9l1sn291i368jn78@group.calendar.google.com)
   1. You can subscribe by clicking the `Add to Google Calendar` button at the bottm left of the regional calendar.
1. You can also subscribe to these calendars directly by using the following ID's
   - Support OOO - AMER - c_9166d2302886c4ae23f34099eeb4015e2d520e1dd4029711becd8370be996513@group.calendar.google.com
   - Support OOO - APAC - c_408bhp8a8j579lqr99j552u21s@group.calendar.google.com
   - Support OOO - EMEA - c_ev56c9rgjd9l1sn291i368jn78@group.calendar.google.com
1. If you regularly handle L&R tickets, please subscribe to the global L&R calendar and relevant L&R regional calendar.

##### L&R and USGov Calendar links

| Group |        |        |        |
| ----- | ------ | ------ | ------ |
| [L&R](https://calendar.google.com/calendar/u/0/embed?src=c_200f3afcbd9d0e18cbd80f00163ea7ca84e08bf857bdafc2bcad4202fed64f3e@group.calendar.google.com) | [APAC](https://calendar.google.com/calendar/u/0/embed?src=c_6d683f9a00d982d28055c0ef986561adc1aacf57570b7285a14ec79c31fd5f89@group.calendar.google.com) | [EMEA](https://calendar.google.com/calendar/u/0/embed?src=c_a849778a4950b23ce10953fa4f98d49e3abdc0aa57e88d448a27d87c6286ad0d@group.calendar.google.com) | [AMER](https://calendar.google.com/calendar/u/0/embed?src=c_55ea946dce89e101efa9d377ae355a201cc96b8d91079ada092cd2d9d821d602@group.calendar.google.com) |
| U.S. Gov | [Daytime](https://calendar.google.com/calendar/u/0?cid=Y182Y2JlZTA4ZmFiOWFjYTI2NzE4YjQ5ODFmOWI5YTk0MDNlNzEyNTRjZmYyZTE5NTc0MjBjN2RhODgwYzg2M2IzQGdyb3VwLmNhbGVuZGFyLmdvb2dsZS5jb20) | [Evenings](https://calendar.google.com/calendar/u/0?cid=Y182MzFiMDNkNGRhYmI3NWZmNjczMDNmMTUwNjZmNTRlYzhhMTE2ZWYzNGE5ZDA4Zjg5YTE1NDJlYzA5YTM5ZjgyQGdyb3VwLmNhbGVuZGFyLmdvb2dsZS5jb20) | [Overnight](https://calendar.google.com/calendar/u/0?cid=Y19hYjlhNzM0ODJmNGM3MDE1NzI0N2EzNTEwYmQxMjdiZWE3ZTExYmUzZWQzN2IzN2FlNThiMjNhOTNhOWI3MjQ3QGdyb3VwLmNhbGVuZGFyLmdvb2dsZS5jb20) |

##### Manager Calendar Links

- [Support Managers AMER](https://calendar.google.com/calendar/embed?src=c_d786d5c8e42ba6058b3a5df60448c17e41255f84a0c00549d197f0466000527d%40group.calendar.google.com&ctz=America%2FChicago)

## Choosing and recording time off

Please take time off whenever you need it.

A little thoughtfulness on everybody's part will go a long way toward making it
possible for everyone to take their desired days off. As you look to plan your
time off, please:

- ensure you know the [company wide paid time off guidelines](/handbook/people-group/time-off-and-absence/time-off-types/)
- consider a different time off schedule if your [regional capacity calendar](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-com/support/toolbox/support-calendar) shows that on any of the days you would be absent, the regional team would be short by 20% or more of its people
- check the regional calendar and coordinate with your manager to ensure we have sufficient cover for days with low availability. You can do this by ensuring that you are subscribed to your associated regional calendar (i.e., `EMEA - OOO`, `AMER - OOO`, `APAC - OOO`) and that prior to booking time off, you check the calendar:
  - 🟩 Green: You're good to book PTO.
  - 🟨 Yellow: The team is nearing PTO capacity – consider other dates if possible.
  - 🟥 Red: PTO capacity has been reached. Please discuss with your manager before proceeding.
  - the calendar colors are determined by the percentage of engineers on PTO:
  - 🟢 Green: 0–15% of engineers on PTO
  - 🟡 Yellow: >15% to 20% of engineers on PTO
  - 🔴 Red: >20% of engineers on PTO
- schedule your time off as far in advance as you can, especially for days that may be popular, are [holidays](#how-support-handles-holidays), or that are particularly important to you
- don't lock yourself into nonrefundable travel itineraries before you've taken steps such as the above to be sure you can get the planned days off
- if possible, plan your time off to avoid disruptions to the various rotations such as on-call

## Preparing for time off

When you are approaching a planned absence from work, it is your responsibility
to take reasonable actions to prepare the team and your customers for your
absence. By making these preparations, you will also be making it easier for
yourself to disconnect from work and make your time off effective.

If you're taking off **less than half a day,** you do not need to make entries in Workday or the Support Time Off Calendar, but please consider updating your Slack status. Also consider blocking the interval on your personal Google Calendar, so no one tries to book a pairing/meeting with you during that time.

If you're taking off **a half day or more,** enter the time off in Workday.

Follow the guidance below to prepare yourself, your customers, and your colleagues.

### Coverage for roles

If you are assigned to any PagerDuty shifts (such as on-call) during the time off, arrange for coverage:

1. Find a volunteer to cover for you; get help from your manager if necessary.
1. [Create the appropriate override in PagerDuty](https://support.pagerduty.com/main/docs/edit-schedules#create-overrides).

### Coverage for assigned tickets

Tidy your queue before going on PTO. As guidelines cannot cover every case,
this section is meant to provide guidance for you to think critically about
what is required to ensure continued excellent support for each customer with
whom you're working on a ticket.

#### If your absence will be less than three business days

If your PTO will prevent a timely update, ask the customer whether
they would prefer to pause the ticket with the `on-hold` status or
have someone else step in.
For high priority tickets, tend towards a handing over to someone else:

1. Use the [OOO Ticket Summary](https://gitlab.com/search?search=360080271299&group_id=2573624&project_id=17008590&scope=&search_code=true&snippets=false&repository_ref=master&nav_source=navbar)
   macro, providing the same information as described in the
   [Workflow](/handbook/support/workflows/ooo-ticket-management#workflow)
   topic of the `OOO Ticket Management` page.

#### If your absence is three or more business days

1. Change your workflow in advance of your absence:
   1. A week in advance: Start thinking about whether you may need to hand off tickets, and pair with others to get them up to speed.
   1. One day in advance: Stop assigning new tickets with your own region as the preferred region. Instead, prioritize FRT-stage tickets from other regions that you can respond to initially and then reassign (reHome) after your first reply.
   1. Work to resolve and close as many of your assigned tickets as possible.
   1. Contribute more to first responses and other people's tickets - internal comments, pairing
      sessions - to make up for not taking new tickets of your own.
1. Follow the [OOO Ticket Management](/handbook/support/workflows/ooo-ticket-management)
   process to arrange for others to take care of your tickets in your absence.
1. To ensure you're not auto-assigned to GDPR requests in case of an extented leave (e.g 2 weeks or longer):

   - Update the corresponding `yaml` file for yourself in the [Support Team project](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-support-readiness/support-team/-/tree/master/data/agents).
   - Change `works_account_deletion: true` to `works_account_deletion: false`
   - Request a review from your manager.
   - Make sure to undo this change when you return from OOO.
1. After coming back, make sure to follow the guidelines for [catching up after a scheduled time off](#catching-up-after-a-scheduled-time-off).

## How Support Handles Family and Friends Days

During [Family and Friends Days](/handbook/company/family-and-friends-day/#upcoming-family-and-friends-days) GitLab Support continues
to operate as normal. In FY26, you are free to take off a total of 4 days at your convenience, to celebrate and record as Family and Friends day.
Please follow the same guidelines as you would in [Choosing and Recording Time Off](#choosing-and-recording-time-off).

## How Support Handles Holidays

During Holidays, GitLab Support continues to operate as normal. Always book holidays as required by your locality. For
non-statutory holidays, please follow the same guidelines as you would in [Choosing and Recording Time Off](#choosing-and-recording-time-off).

From late November through the first week of January, "the holiday season,"
each Support region takes additional steps to coordinate time off so that they
will maintain sufficient staffing levels to meet customer needs.

### APAC

APAC plans for several high-impact holiday periods.  Details of these dates are noted in the [APAC support page](/handbook/support/apac/#holiday-coverage-planning).

For end of year coverage, planning begins in September-October.

This typically involves determining the appropriate coverage based on both the volume of incoming tickets during the holiday period the previous year, and the general ticket volume trend since then.

The team then sign up in the planning issue to provide the necessary coverage by the end of October. This allows time for discussion if anything is at risk.

Other factors taken into account for coverage include:

- L&R expertise
- CEOC, CMOC & Support-Manager on-call coverage - we prefer people covering on-call roles to be working rather than doing it while they are on PTO, so we'll generally seek to swap shifts with those providing coverage
- region coverage - as a wide region, we need to ensure we have sufficient people on in both the first and second halves of the APAC day
- shift coverage for 24/7 support

Previous planning issues can be seen in this [epic](https://gitlab.com/groups/gitlab-com/support/-/epics/252).

### EMEA

The EMEA Support Team plans coverage for several high-impact holiday periods throughout the year, with the two primary planning periods being Easter and the End of year Holiday season.

For each of these periods, EMEA Support Managers will create planning issues such as:

- [EMEA Year End Coverage 2025 - 2026](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-com/support/support-team-meta/-/issues/7194) - planning usually begins 6-8 weeks in advance
- [EMEA Coverage Planning - Easter Long Weekend and the surrounding 2 weeks](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-com/support/support-team-meta/-/issues/5806) - planning usually begins in October

These planning issues include an associated spreadsheet where Support Engineers can share their holiday plans and coordinate coverage. This approach ensures:

- Adequate coverage across all EMEA time zones during holiday periods
- Visibility of team availability well in advance
- Fair distribution of holiday time off
- Sufficient expertise coverage (L&R, CEOC, CMOC, and on-call roles)

Team members are encouraged to add their plans to the spreadsheet as early as possible to facilitate better coordination. While the team aims to accommodate all requested time off, Support Engineers should avoid making firm commitments (such as purchasing nonrefundable travel) until coverage has been confirmed by the management team.

### AMER

AMER Support Managers will create and publish an issue in late September, using
[this template](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-com/support/support-team-meta/-/blob/master/.gitlab/issue_templates/Year%20end%20holiday%20coverage%20AMER.md?ref_type=heads).
In that issue they will invite everyone in AMER Support to use a specified Google
Form to indicate their preferences for days off during the holiday season. Once
the form has closed, around the 15th of October, the AMER Support managers will
quickly determine whether any changes need to be made to anybody's requested
days off.

While it's not very likely that anyone will be asked to work on a day that they
would like to take off, it is possible. For that reason, please don't make any
firm commitments (such as purchasing a nonrefundable travel itinerary) until
the management team sends out notice that the schedule is confirmed.

### Holiday time off ticket management

Guidance around ticket handling over global holiday time off is slightly different, because of the potentially increased impact on the Support team.

The following peak holidays have the greatest potential to affect coverage:

- Australia Day (26-January)
- Republic Day (26-January)
- Anzac Day (25-April)
- International Workers Day (1-May)
- Memorial Day (last Monday in May)
- Independence Day (1-July to 4-July)
- U.S. Thanksgiving Day (4th Thursday of November)
- Immaculate Conception Day (8-Dec)
- Christmas Day, St Stephens Day, Boxing Day, New Years Day and Day After New Years (Period between 24-Dec to 2-Jan)
- Holidays that vary in dates each year that are celebrated in multiple countries:
  - Easter Sunday (late March to early April)
  - Easter Monday (late March to early April)
  - Whit Monday (May or June)
  - Ascension Day (May)
  - Labour Day (first Monday in September)

**NOTE: For AMER holidays and coverage requirements, see [AMER Holiday Coverage Targets](/handbook/support/amer/#amer-holiday-coverage-targets)**.

### If you are planning to take time off during peak holidays

If you plan to be out for more than three days, follow the guidance regarding
[absences of three or more business days](#if-your-absence-is-three-or-more-business-days).
Otherwise:

1. Please do your best to resolve any assigned tickets you have in your queue.
1. Communicate with your customers to let them know the days you'll be away, and
   to ask whether they will need help during your absence. Many of our customers
   might be on the same holiday schedule and will be fine with resuming work on
   a ticket when you both return.
1. For those tickets that will not require action over the holiday, there is no
   special action to be taken.

### If you are working on a holiday

1. Continue to prioritize FRT first, and then management of your own tickets.
1. Please pay **extra** attention to NRT on tickets with an assignee who is currently out-of-office.

## General Tips

In addition to the company-wide tips in
[Communicating Your Time Off](/handbook/people-group/time-off-and-absence/time-off-types/),
take a look at these tips to increase your ability to disconnect from work,
truly make the most of your time off, and make it easier to return to work:

1. Unsubscribe from any MRs that will likely resolve while you're away, and then
   you won't have to deal with all the emails from them when you return.
1. Set up some email filters to move emails into buckets that you can address
   one-at-a-time when you return.
1. Disconnect yourself from Slack and Gmail in any of these ways:
   *NOTE: Time Off by Deel is supposed to turn off Slack notifications on your phone and
   set DND mode. But just in case, you may want to do one of these:*
   1. log out from Slack and Gmail on your phone, or
   1. remove Slack and Gmail from your phone, or
   1. pause the Slack and Gmail apps on your phone
   1. manually configure Slack and Gmail to send no notifications on your phone

## Re-connect after time off

Please consider adding an item in the Support Week in Review after you get back to let the rest of the
team know what you've been up to!

## Catching up after a scheduled time off

Trying to catch-up after a scheduled time off - especially if it's a week long, or more - can be a bit overwhelming.
So here is a list of resources to check that should get you up to date with almost everything
that happened while you were away:

- [Support Week in Review (SWIR)](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-com/support/readiness/support-week-in-review/-/issues/?sort=created_date&state=closed&label_name%5B%5D=SWIR%3A%3ADigest&first_page_size=20)

- Slack channels:
  - [#company-fyi](https://gitlab.slack.com/archives/C010XFJFTHN)
  - [#company-fyi-private](https://gitlab.slack.com/archives/C02E7JGBU4E)
  - [#whats-happening-at-gitlab](https://gitlab.slack.com/archives/C0259241C)

Consider setting up a few coffee chats with teammates to simply reconnect with them. You can also ask your teammates who haven't taken PTO while you were out, during coffee chats or pairing sessions, to mention a thing or two that you might have missed.

If you unassigned some of your tickets before going on PTO, take the time to go through them and check their status. It's good practice to reassign them to yourself if these are either still missing a DRI, or if it appears that you're still the best equipped person to drive it to a solution.

## Managers Time Off

### Before PTO is taken

The manager will conduct a thorough review of all ongoing tasks, responsibilities, and projects.

1. List Key Responsibilities: The manager will prepare a comprehensive list of all tasks that require attention during their absence.
1. Determine Priority: The manager will assess which tasks are time-sensitive and which can be delayed. They will prioritize duties based on urgency, impact, and team dependency.
1. Select a Delegate: The manager will choose a single team member to be responsible for all of the tasks, or another manager if any of the tasks are confidential.

### Task Delegation

Once tasks have been identified and the team member has been selected, the following steps should be taken to ensure a seamless transition:

Documenting the Process: The manager will create an issue to outline

- Key contacts for each task.
- Any ongoing projects or deadlines.
- Specific instructions or checklists to be followed.
- Access to Resources: Ensure that the delegate has the necessary access to tools, files, and systems to perform tasks effectively.

### Communicate

The manager will inform the team and relevant stakeholders about the temporary delegation of responsibilities.

### After PTO

Conduct a Debriefing: The manager will meet with the team member to review the progress made, any challenges encountered, and the outcomes of decisions made in their absence.

For more tips, check [returning from pto](/handbook/people-group/time-off-and-absence/time-off-types/).

## Shift Engineer Time Off

### Planning Coverage for Time Off

Before their time off, Shift Engineers should find coverage for their weekend shifts. The following people should be considered first for covering shifts:

1. Other Shift Engineers.
1. Support Engineers in the CEOC role leading up to the weekend.
1. Other Support Engineers, or ask a Manager for assistance finding coverage.

Coverage is only required for weekends days being taken off. All other days can follow the normal time off recommendations.

### Sick Time

If you are sick, [page the on-call Support Manager](/handbook/support/on-call/#engaging-the-on-call-manager) as soon as you know you will be out on a weekend.

### Guidelines for Covering a Weekend Shift

If you are covering for a Shift Engineer, be mindful of what tickets are allowed to have [public replies](/handbook/support/workflows/working-on-tickets/#weekend-focus-for-shift-engineers) posted during a weekend.

### Holidays as a Shift Engineer

If a holiday occurs on a weekend, and you'd like to take it off, follow the guidance to plan coverage for your time off.

You are also welcome to work the holiday, and float the holiday time to another day of your choosing. It's recommended that you float the holiday to any day within one month before or after the holiday.
